dos.text: Set slot="primary" yourself on a primary button that does not carry primary styling, onSlotchange only auto-promotes a plain <button> with class="primary", type="submit", autofocus or default, or a <moz-button> whose type is primary or destructive.
Assert on slot assignment rather than DOM or visual order in tests, #reorderLightDom() puts primary buttons first on Windows and last everywhere else and render() swaps the two slots to match.

donts.text: Don't set platform in markup, it is declared as { state: true } and assigned by #detectPlatform() in the constructor, so an attribute you write is ignored.
Don't wrap the buttons in a container element, onSlotchange switches on child.localName and only ever promotes button and moz-button, so a wrapper leaves every child in the default slot unordered.
Don't put class="primary" on a <moz-button> expecting promotion, that branch reads the type property instead, so only type="primary" or type="destructive" moves it.
Don't rely on the light-DOM order you authored, #reorderLightDom() calls prepend or append on your own children, so the element rewrites its child order after every slotchange.
